utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, Mr. Jemini, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jemini, we ended yesterday with the question about when you left your family farm. Before we go back to the question that I asked, I would just like to ask you this. In paragraph 28 of your statement of the 17th of July, you say that you did not find the bodies of your family members because gypsies and policemen went down the main road and carried off the bodies, including the bodies of your parents and your relatives. Is it correct what you say in your statement?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement that when I left on the 27th in the morning we did not have the opportunity to go and look at the victims. So we went to Xerxe. The bodies were taken away after that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said, yes, that the gypsies and policemen went down the main road and carried off the bodies and that you were not able to find the bodies of your parents and your relatives because they were not there. But do you recall that on the 21st of October, 1999, you gave a statement to a German forensic team, to the inspectors who were on that team?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the whole time that the German forensic team was in the village, I was with them. We cooperated with them. As I said in the statement. I can't remember exactly now about this thing that you're asking me, but if you are more concrete in your question I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was very specific. Do you remember -- well, if not the date but at least of the fact that you gave a statement to a German forensic team?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember for the moment. I remember that I was with them all the time. We spoke with them and gave them statements, several statements, about the various people and victims; but if you have a concrete question about each and every statement that we gave them, I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I'm asking you very specifically about your parents. Do you remember that you gave a statement to a German forensic team? Is my question clear to you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for the Defence Exhibit D002-5640 to be called up, please. Your Honours, this is a report by the German forensic team dated 21 October, 1999, subject: The murder of the Jemini family and interrogation of Agimi Jemin [as interpreted] born on the 25th November 1960 in Prizren. Inspector Ulrich, Senior Inspector Remmerden, and Chief Inspector Steinmann are signed on the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall now this document? Did I remind you perhaps of this questioning?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Further along in this report it says he was questioned for the purpose of gathering more information about the crime scene. He still remembered the questioning of his brother Jemini Remizija by the group of inspectors on the 28th July.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down and repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, your sentence before last was missed by the interpreters. You are asked to repeated it a little more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The witness also explained that in the refugee camp in Tirana in the spring of that year the investigator of the ICTY John Zdrilic had already questioned him in detail about this murder, therefore we would refrain from further questioning. Have I jogged your memory a little?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, all right. Contrary to the existing statement of the witness, this witness claimed that he had found the bodies of the witness Sadri Jemini, Senavere Jemini, Sahip Jemini, whose bodies had been incinerated in the fire next to the broken-in safe in the bedroom of his parents. Do you remember now?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned in my previous statements that the bodies of the members of my family were not found. They were taken away to Rahovec. We found them in the cemetery in Rahovec, and later on reburied them in the village. I mentioned also that we buried 78 victims from the village, but my family were not among those that we buried at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, please listen to me carefully and listen carefully to what I'm reading and then answer the questions, rather than telling me things that I didn't ask about. We have already wasted the whole day yesterday. Please let me not repeat. I've already read this passage. An inspector of the German forensic team on the 21st October, 1999, noted that these three bodies had burned in the fire in the bedroom of your parents next to the safe that was broken into. Is that correct or not? Please tell me.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Money had been taken by the Serb police from the safe. The safe was in the bedroom. The inspector went there and saw the safe where the police had taken the money from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, you are straining my patience. This is my cross-examination. Please answer my questions very directly. I've just read to you a passage from the report. It says you took the inspectors to the safe in the bedroom and said that the bodies of these three persons had been found there. Is that correct or not? Answer me with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer must be no, Mr. Djurdjic, because that is not what this handwritten report suggests. You have put in additional factors that are not in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm reading what's written. I've read it three times. Whose bodies had burned in the fire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've just put a question to the witness that says that the inspector was taken to the bedroom by the witness, and that is not what is in the report. But the point you're getting at I think is clear. Mr. Jemini, did you at any time find the bodies of Sadri Jemini and the other two members of the Jemini family that have been mentioned by Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but those bodies were found after we returned to Kosova, and they were found in Rahovec. And the Tribunal inspectors exhumed them, conducted the autopsy, and then we reburied them. That's what happened, we reburied them in our village. I think that's very clear. And this can also be confirmed by the inspectors of the Tribunal who came there and took notes of everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did the German police inspectors come after you had returned to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. They couldn't be there during the offensives and the war. They came there in October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it is your recollection that the bodies of these three victims that are named in this German report were found not in the house by a safe in a bedroom, but were found buried at a later date in another place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you or do you have a recollection of saying to the German investigators that these three bodies had been found by you in the burnt house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, does that help you along the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It helped a lot. Perhaps I speeded up the questions that time, but on page 2 of this report it is noted that the witness had taken the police inspectors - that's the third paragraph of the second page in Serbian, and in English it's fourth paragraph - the house in which the three burnt. I'll read this sentence. "Behind the bathroom is the bedroom where, according to the witness's statement, next to a safe box three bodies had been found." And it's signed Chief Criminal Inspector Steiner [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you now know what the -- Mr. Jemini says about that, that he did not find bodies in the house. Now, if you want to ask more about that you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No, I don't want to ask any more. I would just like to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am in a position as pointed out to me, Mr. Djurdjic, that this statement is not a statement of this witness, it's a handwritten report of the German inspector. You want the document tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have what I received from the OTP. It says that the witness is Agim Jemini, born on the 25th of November, 1960, in Prizren. And all the rest are quotations from the words of the witness, signed chief inspector Steiner, and therefore I'm tendering this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received as a record relevant to our inquiry, but don't understand from that, that I at least understand this document to be quoting entirely the words of this present witness. It's a report by the superintendent Steinmann, which brings together his work relating to this. Some of it may be based upon what this witness has said, but clearly much of it is not. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00078, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, in paragraph 27 of your statement you say: "Most of the graves I photographed and the film is in a safe place in Celine. I intend to make it available to the ICTY in The Hague." Thus, in July 1999 you claimed that you photographed the graves. Is this part of the statement correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have told us here something about Hazli making the photographs - let me not repeat what you said about the photographs - but you said that the photographs do not show the graves, they show entirely different.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The photographs show the places where the victims were found, the victims of the massacres immediately after their execution by the Serb forces. And each grave is very close to the place where the execution took place. They are very shallow graves, I think I told you. So in the beginning we filmed -- not filmed, but we photographed the execution site, and then we buried the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I've read to you paragraph 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's the last-but-one paragraph in the witness's statement, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this part of the statement inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is correct. We took pictures and then we buried the bodies, and the ICTY has the pictures. The bodies were buried, and the graves were not filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm reading the statement to you. You only spoke about the graves that were photographed on the 17th of July, 1999, and now you told us at this trial something entirely different, and you gave us photographs that don't show a single grave. Tell us about these graves. Let us not waste time. What about these graves that you mentioned, is this accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're not accurate in what you're asking because the victims were buried. Each and every one of them that we found we took pictures of the massacre, and then we buried them. I think there were some photographs of the graves as well, but if they are missing, what can I do?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I'm not putting a question to you. I read a paragraph from your own statement. It's not a question. I've just read something to you, and I'm asking you to tell me whether it's accurate or not. You are an educated man, an intellectual, you understand my question perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question; however, I think you should understand what the statement says. The statement says that the execution site and the grave-site were photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's not in the statement. I've read it. But let us move on, and the Court will decide. Mr. Jemini, in your statement of the 17th July 1999, there's not a word about a mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked questions about the mosque, and I answered those questions. I don't know how much those answers were reflected in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't find in your statement that you moved tiles from the roof while you were in the loft.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat it again, that maybe in this statement it is not there; however, in my testimony in the previous trials I did mention that we shifted the tiles a little bit in order to be able to see outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you about paragraph 28. Did you see gypsies and policemen gathering bodies on the main road?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did they photograph the bodies before picking them up and putting them on the lorry, the policemen, you know. You know how an on-site investigation is performed. There is the investigation of the crime scene, photographing, collection of clues, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what is normally done in such situations, but these were extraordinary times. And as the events unfolded, I don't think they were thinking about photographing, or I don't think that they had any investigator with them. They just loaded the bodies on the tractor, just like they would load some pieces of wood or rocks. That's what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And these people you call gypsies, were they perhaps members of the civilian defence?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These people had been taken from various places, from Prizren, Rahovec, and other townships. And they did not have any special responsibilities except this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the job of the civilian protection is during the war?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not organise the war to know the duties. I'm telling you what we did on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jemini. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no more strength to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Behar, do you re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, perhaps if Exhibit D77 could be put up on the screen, there's something that you could assist me with. You gave us the name of the person who is in the foreground in this photograph. Could you remind me of that name?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhevdet Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your group throughout this period that you were essentially hiding out and visiting your village in the evenings?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the foreground leaning against a tree appears to be a military automatic weapon. Is that something that was your possession, or did it belong to another member of the group?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapon was there with a group because different weapons were found during that time in the positions of the police in the village. While touring the village in the evening, we found many weapons and ammunition in different positions. This weapon was taken once it was found in one of the positions in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And is it something that you took or another member of the group?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone from the group took it. We did not use that weapon. Some of the members of the group took it, but we didn't use it. We just were curious when we found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you keep it with you for the balance of the period that you were hiding out?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This weapon was perhaps found on that day, when we were photographed on this photograph, but from the photograph you can see where we are, on what kind of location, that we are taking shelter there, and we are not positioned to fight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you find other weapons during the time you were hiding out?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there were weapons in the positions where the military positions were. They did leave traces, such as weapons and ammunition, in their positions that they had in the village. We did take these weapons but not to use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What did you do with the weapons?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did come across different weapons in different positions, in areas where the people had committed massacres, but we didn't take all of them. We didn't take these weapons with us and carry them with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've indicated you took this weapon with you and some others, if I understand you correctly. What did you do with those weapons?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't take other weapons, and this weapon on the photograph was probably in the territory where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what did you do with this weapon?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. We found this weapon right there, and it probably remained right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It wasn't taken from this location by any member of your group?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, Your Honour, we were worried. We had many things on our mind. We felt insecure. We were upset because of the massacres that were committed at that time. That's why I didn't pay attention whether it was taken or left there. But probably it did remain there or was thrown somewhere where it could no longer be used. But we didn't have this weapon with us on other days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, firstly I don't know whether there is anything arising from the Chamber's questioning that you wish to pursue further. Thank you. Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questioning for you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance again in The Hague, for the assistance that you've been able to give. We appreciate the difficulty that you experience in having to recall some of these events, and we express our gratitude for you in what you've been prepared to do. You may now of course return to your normal activities, and the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, you seem to have moved to the front seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The next witness is Hazbi Loku.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Neuner has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your name is Hazbi Loku, and you were born on the 25th of March, 1961.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're a Kosovo Albanian from Kotlina in Kacanik municipality.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you gave a statement on the 4th of June, 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you also testified on the 11th and 12th September, 2006, in the Milutinovic et al case?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And before you came here today, you had an opportunity to review both the statement and the testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And together do the statement and the transcript of testimony truly and accurately reflect what you would say if you gave your testimony orally before this Court today?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring to 65 ter number, that's the statement, 2296, which I would seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00652, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm also referring to the transcript of testimony in the Milutinovic case which has the 65 ter number 5085.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00653, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm reading out the summary of this witness's evidence. On the 8th of March, 1999, the village of Ivaja was shelled, and there was a fight between Serb forces and the villagers. A day later Kotlina, the witness's village, was shelled. The witness observed VJ and police forces entering Kotlina. He saw tanks of a military green colour and dark blue armoured personnel carriers. Most houses in the neighbourhood called Dreshec were burned down. In the other part of Kotlina, shops were looted, houses damaged. Two men were found shot dead. On the 24th of March, 1999, Kotlina was again shelled from different directions. From his hiding point the witness observed a tank firing and a large number of Serb soldiers and policemen capturing and mistreating unarmed male villagers. The captured men were beaten with rifle-butts and kicked. Elderly male villagers were being separated from the women and children, and about 20 men had to lay on the ground. Women and children were loaded onto military lorries and driven in the direction of Kacanik. Some of them had to walk behind the lorries. The elderly men were also taken in the same direction by the Yugoslav Army and policemen. The captured men were taken to a new location where holes were. At the edge of these holes they were beaten. The witness heard the men screaming. All men were thrown into the hole. Later an explosion occurred at this area, and the witness saw dust and a cloud of smoke rising. Other Serb troops started burning the houses in Kotlina. The witness and other villagers found the bodies of Vesel Vlashi and Idriz Kuqi. Zymer Loku died from his wounds later that night. The witness went in a group to Macedonia. End of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you, Mr. Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I have the 65 ter number 615.08 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one question for my learned friend Mr. Neuner. I received the summary of the statement from the Prosecution. And in the first sentence in my summary it says that there was a conflict between the forces, between the Serb forces of the Serb army, and the KLA. And I hear in the interpretation here that there was a conflict between the Serb forces and the villagers. That's what I heard in the interpretation here. That's the 8th of March. That's the only thing that I'm interested in. Is there a problem with the interpretation, or did Mr. Neuner now say the villagers and not the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears Mr. Djurdjic understood from his copy of the summary that there was mention of a conflict between Serb forces and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is certain an issue which my learned colleague is invited to address on cross-examination with any questions he wishes to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you use the word "KLA," or did you use the word "villagers"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I personally used the word "villagers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you explain why a summary would be given to Mr. Djurdjic that mentioned KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can't explain this at this point in time, Your Honours. I can simply say I have not asked this witness during proofing about the fact that, yeah, "KLA" was used in the summary, and I thought therefore because I am summarising his evidence, since I have not asked him in proofing about this particular point, that I should not read it to him that it was the KLA. I thought out of fairness to the witness I say "villagers" here at this point in time. But as I mentioned, my learned colleague is invited to address that issue, and I can even do it now if Your Honours wish me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, the position is clear. Mr. Djurdjic knows it. Either if you choose to, you may explore the question. I suspect certainly Mr. Djurdjic will explore it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, could I just because the question was raised right now, in terms of the conflict in Ivaja on the 8th of March, 1999, have you observed that elements of the KLA were involved in the fightings around Ivaja?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: On the 8th of March, I was in Kotline with the rest of the population, but we were aware that around Ivaja there were KLA soldiers, and we were aware that the Serb forces were fighting them. But they were not in the village of Ivaja; they were in the outskirts of Ivaja village. Personally I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You just said you didn't see the KLA soldiers. What is the basis of your awareness about the KLA presence around Ivaja, as you just stated?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: We are talking about the 8th of March. We heard that on the evening of 8th of March, Reshat [as interpreted] Rexha came to Kotline, and he told us that there was shelling going on in his village, i.e., Ivaja, for the whole day and that the KLA forces in the outskirts of the village were fighting the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Reshat Rexha mention a number of KLA forces?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: No. He had fled his village, and he came to take shelter in our village. He was a young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And had he seen these alleged KLA forces during his flight?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: As he was saying, he did see that with his own eyes. He managed to flee the village during the day and to reach our village, to visit his uncles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I hope, Your Honours, I have clarified and also for the Defence this point now. Therefore, I would go to 65 ter number 61508, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you see in front of you a map.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you, first of all, since we discussed Ivaja, could encircle Ivaja on this map and mark a 1 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Ivaja is this part here. Shall I mark it -- yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The 1 is not very legible. Could you maybe on top of this circle mark another 1, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then your own village, Kotlina, if you could circle this and mark a 2, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Kotlina is to the south of Ivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned in your statement and testimony that artillery was fired on the 9th of March on Kotlina. Could you just by encircling the locations indicate from where the artillery attacks were coming. You just need to --

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The shelling on the 9th of March on Kotline came from these directions. The Serb police forces were positioned here at Gllobocica, then in Gorance or -- they were also positioned on the asphalt road Kacanik-Hani i Elezit main road at the location called Kasha. And shelling was also coming from a position somewhere up -- a little upper from Kacanik; I don't know exactly where. I did circle the locations from where these artillery was active on Kotline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark next to each circle a number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Just number 3, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, next to each circle, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you mentioned that on that occasion also infantry was moving towards Kotlina. Could you by drawing with an arrow indicate from where the infantry troops were coming on the 9th of March.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The infantry troops escorted by the tanks came from the direction of Gllobocica, from the direction of Shtraza, from the direction of Ivaja, from these three directions they came to Kotline, the Serb paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record the witness has marked three arrows indicating the direction of the infantry movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then you mention that on that occasion, 9th of March, Dreshec, the neighbourhood of Kotlina, was affected. Could you by drawing a small circle with a 4 indicate where Dreshec is.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The neighbourhood of Dreshec is west to the centre of Kotline village. It is in the direction of Gllobocica village, about 1 or 2 kilometres far. It should be somewhere here. The road coming from the direction of Gllobocica to our village passes by this neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then on the 24th of March you testified there was another attack. Could you by looking on this map just indicate where were the lines of attack. Don't mark it, just indicate it by telling us which lines of attacks occurred on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: On the 24th of March the shelling continued from the previous positions that I mentioned, where they were positioned, and the infantry came from the same directions because there were no other directions to come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So to clarify, the shelling was coming also from the four points which you have encircled here with number 3?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the infantry attack also from the three arrows which you have indicated here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I seek to tender that map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00654, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just before the map disappears, you stated in your testimony that you were leaving towards Macedonia after the attacks on the 24th of March. Could you indicate where you crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Can I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: On the night of the 24th of March, a group of us who survived the massacres and killings --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You just need to tell me where you crossed the border. That's all I'm asking you for.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: We crossed the border at Gorance village. I marked the road with this arrow. From there we went to Jadrice village which is in Macedonia. We walked throughout the night to get to Jadrice in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And for the record you have drawn a line with an arrow at its end indicating where you were ending up in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I seek to tender this map into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how large your group was when you were crossing the border.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00655, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were more than 40 and less than 50 I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want now to show you another exhibit; it's 5254. And my first question when it will come up in a second is what location, if any, is depicted? It will come up in a second. Just wait, this is -- we just need one screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could enlarge it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What location is depicted here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The picture shows the Kotline village in the municipality of Kacanik. This is the centre of the village. The outer neighbourhoods are not included in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In your testimony and statement you mention that on the 24th of March when Serb forces came to your village you were hiding on a certain location. Could you encircle, if it is shown on this photo, where you were hiding. And mark a 1 next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You then mention in your statement that there was a group of women, children, and elderly on a meadow. Could you encircle where you saw that group of women, children, and elderly and a few men. Mark a 2 inside the circle if you can.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you also mentioned a group of about 20 men which were, so to speak, captured somewhere else. Could you mark where that group was.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you could next to that circle mark a 3, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I would like to show from you is on the position you mark as number 1, in terms of elevation is that position on the same elevation as number 2 and 3? Is it higher or lower?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The location at number 1 is at the same elevation as number 3, while number 2, the fields and the houses are lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you mention in your testimony that the group you marked here with number 3 is being led to wells or holes. Could you encircle and mark with number 4 where the holes are if they are depicted on this picture.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I seek to tender that exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00656, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to revert to the exhibit that's the statement which I just tendered, it's Exhibit 652, and want to have the last page of that exhibit, it's page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who produced this drawing?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I produced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what does this drawing reflect?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The drawing depicts the village of Kotline; the road; the houses; the roads that come from the direction of Ivaja-Shtraza-Gllobocica; the main buildings; the mosque; the clinic; the place where I was staying, where I have marked as "kalaja," which means the castle, there are the ruins of a castle there; the place where the people were executed and massacred, my co-villagers and members of my family --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop you here. Is it fair to say that this handwritten drawing reflects the same excerpt which we have seen a moment ago in form of a photo?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I tried to depict the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could zoom in a little bit on the upper left-hand side of that picture -- of the drawing. Even a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here on the upper left-hand side the word above circle "gropa"?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you spell for the record "gropa."

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The word "gropa" means wells or holes, a person from the village who wanted to get water for his family --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I was just asking you to spell the word "gropa" for the record.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: G-r-o-p-a, "gropa."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, previously my learned friend said - at least I heard in interpretation - "group." And now the witness is telling us that "gropa" means well. Therefore, the words written here in Albanian seems to mean a well. Then the witness was interrupted at that point in order to spell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We won't interfere, Mr. Neuner, in your examination. It will be up to you whether you want to explore that matter; if you don't, Mr. Djurdjic will.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I've only one question -- two questions. Is "gropa" singular or plural in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The word "gropa" in Albanian is in plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How would you spell for the record a -- the word -- the singular word for "hole"?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: In singular I would say, g-r-o-p-e, "grope."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This exhibit could be removed, please. I would like to show the witness 65 ter number 48, please. And we just need one screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There will be three pictures coming up now. And the first question I will always ask you is who gave these pictures to the ICTY? If you could -- I think it needs to be moved, yeah. If you could answer that question first, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I gave this photograph to the Tribunal myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When was this picture taken?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This picture was taken after we returned from Macedonia. This is the picture of the school of the village where I used to work. You can see here that the school had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you give me year and approximate month in which you returned from Macedonia to take this picture?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This picture was taken around August or September 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I seek to tender that picture, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00657, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you left the village Kotlina to move to Macedonia, in what condition was the school?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Up until the 23rd of March, the school was a building where pupils went and studied; and then on the 24th of March it was burnt down, together with other houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see it being burnt, or was the school intact when you left the village?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I did see it with my own eyes during the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As being intact or ...

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: In the morning it was intact. When the Serb forces came, in the afternoon, the school was torched.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next picture is 0050.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I need to tender the previous -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who gave this picture to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When was this picture taken?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The picture was taken in the beginning of September 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm now referring to, on the right-hand side, the house without roof. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: On the right you can see that there are several houses that had been burnt on the 24th of March. There are many burnt houses here if you look at the picture carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then there is one house which is in the middle of this picture with a light roof, wooden roof. What can you tell us about this house?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is Nuredin Kuqi's house. The walls were not burnt down. Then there was a humanitarian organisation that came and helped our village, and they helped us build the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when was the roof burned on that house?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This house was burnt on the same day, on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I seek to tender that picture, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00658, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I have 65 ter number 380. This is a collection of pictures, and I'm just asking you who gave these pictures to us.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I brought these photographs as a testimony to the most cruel killings that were committed by the Serb forces and Yugoslav forces in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to provide us the names of the person, and I will go through these pictures one by one. Upper row to the left, just tell us who the persons depicted -- depicted there is.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Starting from the right to the left, the first one is Adnan Refik Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Upper row to the middle?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person in the middle is Naser Rexhep Loku, the third one is Mina Baki Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could just answer the questions I'm putting to you. I'm asking for specific persons. The middle row, the man in the middle, who is this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: In the first row --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No, in the middle row, the man in the middle.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Naser Rexhep Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then in the lower row, the man to the left?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: These two are two brothers, Ibush Rexhep Loku and Naser Rexhep Loku, two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I just asked you for one person's identity, and you're giving me two. In the lower row on the left-hand side, what is the name of this person in the dark black jacket with a beard? What's the name of him?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, with a moustache, this is Sali Vlashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the lower row in the middle, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person in the middle is -- as I said, they are two brothers. One is Ibush, the other is Naser. Maybe I confused their names, but I know that one of the brothers is called Naser and the other Ibush.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then if we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Upper left-hand side, who is this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Upper left-hand side, this person is Danush Kuqi. He was a student in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand side, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is Sherif Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the lower left-hand side, who is this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Xhemajl Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The lower right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Vesel Vlashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who is the person on the upper left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person on the upper left-hand side is Ferat Kuqi's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The person there on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This person is Garip Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the person on the lower left-hand-hand -- lower right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This person is his son, Sabit Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the persons which have just been identified by this witness are listed in Schedule K of the indictment, and with this examination I seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00659, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. This would appear to be a convenient time for us to have the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just apologise, I must have overlooked the last page, and I'm really sorry. I must have overlooked the last page of this exhibit because there is still six persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have it back on the screen, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I apologise also to the witness. Yes. Witness, if you could be so kind and identify the person on the upper left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person in the upper left-hand side is Agim Loku, Nazmi Loku's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the person in the upper middle?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is Ismail Loku, Agim's brother, Agim Loku's brother. They were two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The person in the upper right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Ismail Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The lower right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is Zymer Loku. He was about 70 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The person on the lower middle?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person in the middle is my brother, Milaim Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the person of the lower right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is Reshat Rexha from Ivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could also - thank you. If this exhibit can be removed - ask that Exhibit 360 is shown to this witness, another picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is depicted here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This picture depicts the holes that we mentioned earlier from where we got the bodies of the people that we saw in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you say a little bit -- who provided it to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I gave this picture to the Tribunal, together with the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what time of the year was this picture approximately taken?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: That was late fall or maybe early spring when there were no leaves on the trees, maybe February or March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you yourself taken that picture?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I seek to tender this exhibit into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 00360 would be assigned P00660, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That being so, we will have the first break now. We must have a break at this time to enable the tapes to be rewound which takes half an hour. So we'll resume at 11.00. The court officer will show you after we have adjourned where to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djurdjic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Loku, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. With me is my associate Ms. Marie O'Leary; she is a member of our team as well. Now I would like to ask you to listen carefully to my questions and to answer as briefly as you can. If you don't understand my question, please tell me, and I will try to clarify. Now I would like us to go back, if we can, to P6562 [as interpreted], page 9. Mr. Loku, here is there just one circle that is drawn in where you say "gropa"?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, what does it mean when it says g-r-o-p-a-e and when it is written g-r-o-p-e-s in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: "Gropa," as I have written it on the sketch, is in plural, meaning two or more holes, whereas "gropes" has no meaning in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to look at Exhibit P652. And if possible I would like to have the Albanian and the English version on the screen. Page 6, please in the Albanian version. In English it's the end of page 5, but I think that what I'm actually interested in is on page 6 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, can you see in the Albanian version at the beginning of the page, then it's the fourth paragraph on that page. It ends with the words "gropes." In the Serbian translation, and I believe in the English translation, it -- it is "hole" in the singular.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, I do read it. It's clear. It says: "After these groups had left," the groups refer to the groups of people that had gathered in the fields of the village, "groups" refers to a group of people. It has nothing to do with "grope" which in English is "holes" and "wells."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, that's the second sentence: "And then I saw the captured men being led away towards where I knew there was a large hole."

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, does it say here, this thing that I read out?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to "holes."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And "hole" or "holes"? I have the version that says hole in the singular, and that's why I'm asking you whether in the Albanian it's in the singular or in the plural.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Here it is in singular with the "e" in the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the end of the same paragraph, the last-but-one sentence reads: "30 minutes later from the area of the hole," again is it just one hole, singular?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: It's again in singular here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then two sentences further up it says: "I saw the first two villagers thrown into the hole." Is it again in singular?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: It's again in singular here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now get -- in English it's page 6, and in the Albanian language it's page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the first sentence it says: "I spoke to Rexhep Loku who remained in my village, and he has told me that on the edge of the hole ..."

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's at page 7 in the Albanian version, the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in my version it says: "I spoke to Rexhep Loku, who remained in my village, and he told me that on the edge of the hole ..." Is it one hole, singular, here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Sometimes it is in singular and sometimes in plural. In the statement there are cases when it is written with "a," "gropa," and then when it is written with "e" for singular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I asked you about paragraph 27. I never found any mention of the word ending in an "a." I did find mention of the word ending with an "e." So I'm asking you about 27th paragraph, it's the third paragraph from the bottom in the Albanian language, is it in the singular or in the plural here? You can see that Rexhep Loku is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: It is in singular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And it says "gropes," it's the singular, but I suppose it's in a different case, "buze gropes."

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, it says "gropes."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that means "at the edge of the hole" when you translate it, "buze gropes," that's what it means?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Well, Exhibit P360 is a picture, but I thought first that we wouldn't have to look at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but do put it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not the one. 360, P. It's the picture of two wells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My friend could perhaps assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think you were referring to 65 ter number 360, which I have noted down as P660, Exhibit P660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall what year this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This photograph was taken after the events, that is, after we returned from Macedonia where we stayed as refugees. I did not note down the date, but it should be in 1999/2000, after we returned from Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, where were you when you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken from the direction where I was hiding, from where I could see the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What camera did you use to take this photograph, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: A digital camera that I had at home. I don't know the name of the model, but that's a camera we used in my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How -- what is the elevation of the spot from which you took this photograph above sea level, if you know that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But from what I can see on this photograph, do you agree that that spot would be higher than the area where those holes are?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: No, it's not higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, are those two holes lower or at the same height as the place from which you took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The place from where I took this photograph is lower than the place of the two holes, but these two holes cannot be seen from above but from the side. They can be seen from the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered my question. But can you explain to me, was there a wooded area at the position from which you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: There were trees, but -- oak trees, but not so many. The old fortress is nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me when did you hand-over this photograph and to whom did you hand it over?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I brought these photographs here. I don't know to whom I hand them over. When I came here to testify before the Tribunal, I took them with me and handed them over. I don't remember the name of the person whom I gave them to. I brought many photographs, not only these ones that we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can see two dots here. It's obviously a photograph that has already been used in a different trial. I think you testified in both the Milosevic and the Milutinovic trials. And did you put those dots here the first time that you came here or the second time?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: What do you mean, dots?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can see two red dots. It's usually the witnesses who do that. Do you see it on the photograph? To the left of the first hole and above the second hole; it's red circles. Usually this is the kind of markings that witnesses make here using the pen.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The red dots, they are not dots. They are the national flags of Albania. These are two flags placed on each side of the holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, of course. I'm sorry. I do apologise. But do you remember when you handed over those photographs for the first time?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just have one more question regarding this photograph. So you rule out the possibility that this photograph was given to you by the Austrian forensic team?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: As I said, I brought many photographs here. One of them is this one that we are looking at. There are photographs that I took myself with my camera, there were also other photographs. As I said, there were many photographs. Now, whether this is the one that I took personally, that I don't know, but it resembles the one that I took myself. It's taken from the same position and depicts the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you recall the arrival of the Austrian forensic team?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time when they came. Many teams came, teams from KFOR, from UNMIK, a Norwegian team, a Swiss team came. Many teams came to inspect the site where the events occurred, but the team that exhumed these two holes, I think it had Austrian -- it comprised of Austrians, and there was some Norwegians, too, as part of that team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Loku. Mr. Loku, at the beginning of your testimony today you told my learned friend, Mr. Neuner, that on the 8th of March there had been shelling from the location that you mentioned, Kasa, Kacanik, Gorance. And you said that those had been the Serb police forces, that they did the shelling. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: We knew that because we had seen these forces on those positions for months when we would travel around the local roads and pass through their check-points. The army also had sort of a barracks at Gllobocica because that's where the border with Macedonia is. The borderline from Gllobocica to Hani i Elezit, along this line there were also military forces of the former Yugoslavia stationed there, and in the northern part that I pointed out there were also Serb forces positioned. We could see these forces when we would go to Kacanik, on our way to Kacanik and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, how do you know how far those forces were from your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: They were not positioned very far. The village of Gllobocica is about 4 or 5 kilometres far from our village as the crow flies. Then the position at Kashan is also less than 4 or 5 kilometres as the crow flies far from our village. The third position is also about 4 kilometres far as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how about Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Kacanik is a little bit further, about 12 or 13 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Visually when you are in Kotlina, do you see these places you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: You can see three of these places from Kotlina, Gllobocica, Kashan, and Gorance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: With a naked eye?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, with a naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And from what artillery piece did they shell?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: At two of the positions that I passed by very often, Gllobocica and Kashan positions, I saw tanks positioned there, and we did see shells falling in the outskirts of the village. I think that these shells came from these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And these tanks, they were what colour?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: They were Yugoslav Army tanks, green.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I call up Defence Exhibit D002-5868. Image number 3 first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe this image, Mr. Loku?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the gravestone of Mahi Loku, Mahi Shefedin Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where is this tombstone?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: This is in the martyrs' cemetery in Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the tombstone are there any symbols?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: As I said, this is the martyrs' cemetery in the municipality of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the late person depicted in uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The person when he was killed, he was in civilian clothes. However, when they were depicted here in the tombstone, the photographs were the same. They were depicted in the same way as far as clothes are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And to cut the long story short, on all the other photographs there is an engraved coat of arms of the KLA, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: All of them have the KLA emblem, and the uniforms were drawn, these uniforms were from the KLA, both the uniforms and the emblems were engraved on the tombstone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the photograph number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose tombstone this is.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the grave of Sabri Hamid Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have image number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness, that this is Adnan Loku's grave?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is. His gravestone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image number 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that on this photo we see the tombstone of Neshat Rexha?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it struck me, is that the same person you mentioned today when my learned friend asked you who was the first to give you the news of the events in Ivaja?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, this is the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us clear up one more thing, although I believe there are many more errors. His exact name, can you tell us how to read it in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: His name on the tombstone is Neshat. Whether it was Reshat or Neshat, I wasn't sure at the time, but he is the same person. He is the son of Ferat Rexha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was image 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Image number 7, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is the name of Abush Loku on the tombstone?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, Abush Loku, a martyr from the village of Kotline.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 9, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it Xhemajl Kuqi?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, Xhemajl Nuredin Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I call up Defence Exhibit D002 -- in fact, I should have asked to tender the -- this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is the images that you've identified and had shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Pages 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 of e-court, Your Honours, of D002-5868 will be assigned D00079.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may I call up D002-5879, please. Image 9, please, first. I think that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what we see on this picture.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Here you can see part of the Kotline village. The picture is taken from the road from Kashan that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All this greenery and the hill in the background of the picture, is it where the holes were, the ones we talked about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The green area above the village is the place where the young people of the village had been grouped together and where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you encircle the place where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The picture was taken after the foliage came on, so if I am -- if I am correct, the place should be somewhere here, the place where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you are right. And now I'd like to know -- please don't draw anything. Just tell me, are you able to determine the location where you were then? Is it visible here? No, no, please don't take the pen. Just --

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The place I was staying is not here in the photograph. It's on the right part of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So if we look to the right of the photograph ...

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Well, as I see the photograph, the place is to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We just need to describe the way we see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the red [sic] circle is the witness's mark for the area, the location where the holes were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Loku. So your location was to the left outside this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have image number -- first may I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could just say, it's probably a transcript error, it's a blue circle, not a red circle, as is depicted in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you, it's a slip of the tongue on my part.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00080, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up image 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, do you recognise the location depicted here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: If you can, please don't show me photographs with vegetation because I cannot see anything here for the moment. I can see some oak trees, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the location where the holes were? It's even closer than the first photo.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is from closer up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now encircle the place where these people were in the woods?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: The place where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just for the transcript let me say that the witness put a blue circle on the photo, and I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00081, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The image 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, is the place with the holes even more visible here?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: Yes, it is more visible. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you encircle it again.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where do you think this photograph was taken from? Was it a location higher or lower than the ground shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I first ask my learned colleague to ask who was taking this picture. I mean, if the witness has taken this picture he can certainly speak about it, but to the Prosecution it's unclear that this witness has taken this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Neuner, it's not the witness who took this photograph. It's my colleague, Tomislav Visnjic, who took it. And these photographs were used in the Milutinovic case, and they are in evidence in that case. But I asked the witness about the photograph, about whether it was taken from a higher or a lower ground than the ground shown or maybe from the same level.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could be the same level or lower than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00082, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Image 7, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, this seems to be a close-up of the place. I'd like to say that the photographs seen before were taken on the 24th of May, but I don't know the year. This is now a close-up, a zoom-in; right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: It resembles it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are you sure, or do you think it is?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note for the record that the witness put a blue circle around the location where there were holes in the ground, and I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00083, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, P361, may I call this exhibit up. This is already an exhibit. It has a P number. It's the report of the Austrian forensic team. Witness, on page 6, paragraph 24, of your statement you said -- sorry, it's a 65 ter statement. You said --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
